source.text: יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהַי֙ אַתָּ֔ה אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עָשִׂ֖יתָ פֶּ֑לֶא עֵצ֥וֹת מֵֽרָח֖וֹק אֱמ֥וּנָה אֹֽמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, my God [are] you; I will exalt you, I will give thanks to your name, for you have done wonder[s], plans from distant [time], faithfulness, firmness.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my God [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I will exalt {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done a wonder, plans from long ago, faithfulness [and] firmness.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, you are my God! I will lift {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} high and give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. You have worked a marvel: purposes formed long ago, carried out with steadfast faithfulness.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, you are my God. I will honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. You have done amazing things. You planned them long ago, and you have been completely faithful in carrying them out.

decisions.choice: my God ... I will exalt you: words from the song of the sea
decisions.reason: Exodus 15:2 joins the same two ideas: "this is my God ... and I will exalt him." The song that follows the fall of the city (verse 2) is modeled on Israel's song after the crossing of the sea, as 12:2 is.

decisions.choice: a wonder: a marvel only God can do
decisions.reason: The word is used for God's mighty acts at the exodus (Exodus 15:11; Psalm 77:12) and in the royal child's name "Wonder Counselor" (9:5), which also joins wonder with counsel or plans, as here.

decisions.choice: plans from long ago, faithfulness, firmness: God's ancient purposes carried out with complete reliability
alternatives: plans from long ago, faithful and true (as a description of the plans)
decisions.reason: "From afar" refers to time: God planned this long before (22:11; 37:26). The last two nouns come from the same root, which means to be firm or sure; set side by side they stress that the plans were carried out faithfully and without fail.

decisions.choice: carried out with steadfast faithfulness (Balanced); you have been completely faithful in carrying them out (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the nouns side by side without a verb; Balanced and Readable supply "carried out" to show how the plans and the faithfulness belong together.

source.text: כִּ֣י שַׂ֤מְתָּ מֵעִיר֙ לַגָּ֔ל קִרְיָ֥ה בְצוּרָ֖ה לְמַפֵּלָ֑ה אַרְמ֤וֹן זָרִים֙ מֵעִ֔יר לְעוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א יִבָּנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have made from a city into a heap, a town fortified into a ruin, a fortress of strangers from a city; forever it will not be rebuilt.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made a city into a heap, a fortified town into a ruin, a fortress of foreigners [so that it is] no [longer] a city; it will never be rebuilt.
en.B: You have reduced a city to a mound of stones and a walled town to rubble. The palace-fort of foreigners has stopped being a city; no one will ever build it again.
en.R: You turned a city into a pile of stones. You ruined a town that had strong walls. The fortress where foreigners lived is no longer a city. It will never be built again.

decisions.choice: a city: an unnamed city of the proud
decisions.reason: The city is not named, here or in 24:10, 26:5 and 27:10. Isaiah 24-27 speaks of a city that stands for the whole proud world set against God. Readers have suggested Babylon (chapters 13-14) or Moab, which is judged in verses 10-12, but the text leaves the city unnamed.

decisions.choice: a fortress of strangers: a stronghold of foreign enemies
decisions.reason: The word means a fortified palace or citadel (13:22; 23:13). "Strangers" are foreign enemies, as in 1:7 and verse 5.

decisions.choice: palace-fort
decisions.reason: The word names a building that is both a palace and a fortress; "palace-fort" keeps both.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֖ן יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ עַם־עָ֑ז קִרְיַ֛ת גּוֹיִ֥ם עָרִיצִ֖ים יִירָאֽוּךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore they will honor you, a people strong; a town of nations ruthless, they will fear you.

en.L: Therefore a strong people will honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; a town of ruthless nations will fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: So a mighty people will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} glory; the city of brutal nations will stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: That is why a powerful people will honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. A city of cruel nations will fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: a strong people will honor you: the nations who once opposed God come to honor him
decisions.reason: The strong and ruthless are not Israel but the nations. Seeing God bring down the proud city, they honor and fear him, as the nations turn to God in 2:2-4 and 19:21-25.

decisions.choice: fear you: revere and stand in awe
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to be afraid, but beside "honor" it means the awe that leads to worship (Psalm 22:24).

source.text: כִּֽי־הָיִ֨יתָ מָע֥וֹז לַדָּ֛ל מָע֥וֹז לָאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּצַּר־ל֑וֹ מַחְסֶ֤ה מִזֶּ֨רֶם֙ צֵ֣ל מֵחֹ֔רֶב כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ עָרִיצִ֖ים כְּזֶ֥רֶם קִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have been a refuge for [the] poor, a refuge for [the] needy in his distress, a shelter from rainstorm, a shade from heat, for [the] breath of ruthless [ones] [is] like a rainstorm [against] a wall.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been a stronghold for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in his distress, a shelter from [the] rainstorm, a shade from [the] heat; for the breath of [the] ruthless [is] like a rainstorm [against] a wall.
en.B: You have been a fortress for the weak, a fortress for the needy when trouble pressed on them, cover from the downpour and shade from the scorching sun. The blast of tyrants is like a storm battering a wall.
en.R: You have been a safe place for poor people, a safe place for needy people in their trouble. You are like a shelter in a rainstorm and like shade from the heat. Cruel people attack with fury, like a rainstorm pounding against a wall.

decisions.choice: a stronghold for the poor: God protects those who have no other protection
decisions.reason: The poor and needy are those with no power of their own (11:4; 14:30, 32). God is their stronghold and shelter, as in Psalm 46:2. The pictures of shelter from storm and shade from heat appear again in 4:6 and 32:2.

decisions.choice: the breath of the ruthless: their furious blast
decisions.reason: The word means breath, wind or spirit. Here it is the angry rage of tyrants, which strikes like a driving storm.

decisions.choice: a rainstorm against a wall: the received text
decisions.reason: The received text reads "a storm of a wall", that is, a storm beating against a wall. With one vowel changed the same consonants read "a storm of cold", a winter storm, which would match "heat" in verse 5. The text as it stands makes sense and is kept.

decisions.choice: Cruel people attack with fury
decisions.reason: Readable explains "breath" as the fury with which tyrants attack.

source.text: כְּחֹ֣רֶב בְּצָי֔וֹן שְׁא֥וֹן זָרִ֖ים תַּכְנִ֑יעַ חֹ֚רֶב בְּצֵ֣ל עָ֔ב זְמִ֥יר עָֽרִיצִ֖ים יַעֲנֶֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Like heat in a dry land, [the] uproar of strangers you will subdue; heat by [the] shade of a cloud, [the] song of ruthless [ones] it will be brought low.

en.L: Like heat in a dry land, the uproar of foreigners {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} subdue; [like] heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the ruthless is brought low.
en.B: As heat bakes parched ground, so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring down the roar of foreigners; the way a passing cloud's shade takes the edge off the heat, the tyrants' song of triumph dies away.
en.R: Foreign enemies roar like the heat in a dry desert, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stop their noise. A cloud's shade cools the heat; in the same way {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} silence the songs of cruel people.

decisions.choice: like heat ... heat by the shade of a cloud: the enemy's noise is like heat, and God quells it as cloud shade cools the ground
decisions.reason: The verse has two similes with few words. In the first, the uproar of the foreigners is like the heat of a desert; in the second, God quiets it the way the shadow of a cloud brings relief from heat. It takes up the shade of verse 4.

decisions.choice: the song of the ruthless: their song of victory
decisions.reason: The word usually means a song (24:16). A word with the same spelling means a pruned branch (compare 18:5), and some read "the branch of the ruthless is cut down". The song fits the uproar of the first line.

decisions.choice: is brought low: is silenced
decisions.reason: The verb means to be bowed down or humbled (31:4); said of a song, it falls silent.

source.text: וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת לְכָל־הָֽעַמִּים֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה מִשְׁתֵּ֥ה שְׁמָנִ֖ים מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה שְׁמָרִ֑ים שְׁמָנִים֙ מְמֻ֣חָיִ֔ם שְׁמָרִ֖ים מְזֻקָּקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will make, Yahweh of hosts, for all the peoples on mountain this a feast of fat things, a feast of old wines, fat things full of marrow, old wines refined.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will make for all the peoples on this mountain a feast of rich foods, a feast of aged wines, rich foods full of marrow, aged wines well refined.
en.B: On this mountain {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will spread a banquet for all the peoples: a feast of the richest food, a feast of wine long aged, dishes rich with marrow, old wine strained clear.
en.R: Here on Mount Zion {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will prepare a great feast for people from every nation. There will be the best food and the finest old wine, rich meat and pure, clear wine.

decisions.choice: on this mountain a feast: the meal on Mount Zion after the LORD begins to reign
decisions.reason: "This mountain" is Mount Zion, where the LORD reigns in 24:23. As the elders of Israel ate and drank before God on Sinai (Exodus 24:9-11), so now the nations eat at his table. Jesus speaks of many coming from east and west to feast in the kingdom (Matthew 8:11).

decisions.choice: fat things full of marrow, aged wines refined: the finest food and drink
decisions.reason: Rich, fatty food and marrow were the best portions of a feast. The wines are wine left to mature on its dregs and then strained clear (Jeremiah 48:11; Zephaniah 1:12), the best wine there was.

decisions.choice: for all the peoples: the nations are guests at God's feast
decisions.reason: The feast is not for Israel alone. The peoples who stream to Zion in 2:2-4 are the guests here (56:7).

decisions.choice: Here on Mount Zion
decisions.reason: Readable names the mountain that "this mountain" points to (24:23).

source.text: וּבִלַּע֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה פְּנֵֽי־הַלּ֥וֹט׀הַלּ֖וֹט עַל־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים וְהַמַּסֵּכָ֥ה הַנְּסוּכָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will swallow up on mountain this the surface of the covering, the [one] covering over all the peoples, and the woven [thing], the [one] woven over all the nations.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will swallow up on this mountain the face of the covering that covers all the peoples, and the woven [veil] that is woven over all the nations.
en.B: On this mountain {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will swallow up the veil drawn over the faces of all the peoples, the cloth woven across all the nations.
en.R: Here on this mountain {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy the covering that hangs over all peoples. He will take away the cloth that is spread over every nation.

decisions.choice: swallow up: do away with completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to swallow, and so to destroy completely. It is used again at the start of verse 8, where what is swallowed is death itself.

decisions.choice: the covering over all the peoples: the shroud of grief and death
decisions.reason: The covering is not named. Mourners covered their heads and faces (2 Samuel 15:30; 19:5), and verse 8 goes on to death and tears, so it is most likely the veil of mourning and death that lies over every nation. Paul speaks of a veil over the mind that is taken away in Christ (2 Corinthians 3:14-16), which some see here.

decisions.choice: destroy (for "swallow up")
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of the picture; verse 8 keeps "swallow up" so that the New Testament quotation can be recognized.

source.text: בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֨וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וּמָחָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה דִּמְעָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־פָּנִ֑ים וְחֶרְפַּ֣ת עַמּ֗וֹ יָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: He will swallow up death to perpetuity, and he will wipe away, Lord Yahweh, tear[s] from on every face, and the reproach of his people he will remove from on all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken.

en.L: He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will wipe away tears from every face, and the reproach of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remove from all the earth, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.B: He will swallow up death for all time. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will wipe every face clean of tears and lift from all the earth the disgrace of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.R: He will swallow up death and put an end to it forever. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will dry the tears from everyone's face. He will take away the shame of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people everywhere on earth. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said this will happen.

decisions.choice: he will swallow up death: God destroys death itself
decisions.reason: In the world around Israel, Death was pictured as a swallower with an open throat (5:14; Habakkuk 2:5; Proverbs 1:12). Here the swallower is swallowed. Paul quotes this line in 1 Corinthians 15:54 as fulfilled when the dead are raised.

decisions.choice: forever
decisions.reason: The phrase means for all time (13:20; 28:28; 33:20). Paul's quotation reads "in victory", following a Greek rendering of the word; the root can carry the idea of victory in later Hebrew and Aramaic.

decisions.choice: wipe away tears ... remove the reproach of his people: grief and disgrace ended
decisions.reason: Revelation 7:17 and 21:4 take up these words: God will wipe away every tear, and death will be no more. The reproach of God's people is the shame of defeat and exile, which the nations mocked (Joel 2:17).

decisions.choice: and put an end to it forever
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of swallowing, quoted in 1 Corinthians 15:54, and adds what it means: death is ended.

source.text: וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא הִנֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֥ינוּ זֶ֛ה קִוִּ֥ינוּ ל֖וֹ וְיֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נוּ זֶ֤ה יְהוָה֙ קִוִּ֣ינוּ ל֔וֹ נָגִ֥ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָ֖ה בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And someone will say in that day, Here! our God [is] this; we have waited for him and he will save us. This [is] Yahweh; we have waited for him; let us be glad and let us rejoice in his salvation.

en.L: And it will be said in that day: Look, this [is] our God; we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us. This [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; let us be glad and rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} salvation.
en.B: On that day people will say: Look, this is our God! We waited for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue us. This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one we waited for; let us be full of joy and delight in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} salvation.
en.R: At that time people will say: Look! This is our God! We waited and hoped for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us. This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! We waited for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Let us be happy and celebrate, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought us salvation.

decisions.choice: this is our God ... this is Yahweh: pointing to God who has come
decisions.reason: "This" points to someone present, as when the cities of Judah are told "Here is your God" (40:9). The people greet God, who has come in person.

decisions.choice: we have waited for him: waited in hope
decisions.reason: The verb means to wait with eager expectation, trusting God to act (8:17; 40:31).

decisions.choice: people will say
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject ("one will say"); Balanced and Readable say "people". Literal has "it will be said".

source.text: כִּֽי־תָנ֥וּחַ יַד־יְהוָ֖ה בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְנָ֤דוֹשׁ מוֹאָב֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו כְּהִדּ֥וּשׁ מַתְבֵּ֖ן בְּמ֥וֹ מַדְמֵנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For it will rest, the hand of Yahweh, on mountain this, and it will be trampled down, Moab, in its place, as is trampled down a heap of straw in a dunghill.

en.L: For the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rest on this mountain, and Moab will be trampled down in its place as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.
en.B: The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rest upon this mountain, but Moab will be crushed underfoot on its own ground, like straw stamped down into a dung heap.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will protect this mountain with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power. But Moab will be crushed in its own land, like straw that is stamped down into a pile of animal waste.

decisions.choice: the hand of Yahweh will rest: his power stays to protect
decisions.reason: God's hand stretched out means judgment (5:25; 10:4). A hand that rests on a place shows his power settled there to protect it, here Mount Zion.

decisions.choice: Moab: the proud neighbor, brought down
decisions.reason: Moab lay east of the Dead Sea and was known for its pride (16:6). The word for dung pit sounds like Madmen, a town of Moab (Jeremiah 48:2), so the picture also plays on Moab's own place names.

decisions.choice: in a dung pit: the reading tradition
alternatives: in the water of a dung pit
decisions.reason: The word read aloud means "in"; the written text has a word meaning "in the waters of", which would give "as straw is trampled in the water of a dung pit". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: will protect this mountain with his power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's hand resting on the mountain.

source.text: וּפֵרַ֤שׂ יָדָיו֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְפָרֵ֥שׂ הַשֹּׂחֶ֖ה לִשְׂח֑וֹת וְהִשְׁפִּיל֙ גַּֽאֲוָת֔וֹ עִ֖ם אָרְבּ֥וֹת יָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will spread out his hands in its midst just as he spreads out, the swimmer, to swim, and he will bring low his haughtiness with the tricks of his hands.

en.L: And he will spread out his hands in its midst as the swimmer spreads [them] out to swim, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring low his pride together with the tricks of his hands.
en.B: There Moab will spread out its hands, as a swimmer spreads them out to swim, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring its pride down, for all the cunning of its hands.
en.R: Moab will stretch out its arms in that filth, like someone trying to swim. But God will bring down Moab's pride, no matter how clever its hands are.

decisions.choice: he will spread out his hands: Moab, flailing in the dung pit
alternatives: God spreads his hands in Moab's midst
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. Moab is the last one named, sinking in the pit of verse 10 and trying to swim out of it. The subject may instead be God, who spreads his hands in Moab's midst as a swimmer pushes the water aside, to strike it down.

decisions.choice: the tricks of his hands: Moab's clever schemes
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It most likely means craft or trickery: God brings Moab's pride low together with all its scheming. It may instead mean the strokes of the swimmer's hands, which do not save him.

decisions.choice: Moab (Balanced, Readable); God (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses only "he". Balanced and Readable name Moab as the swimmer; Readable also names God as the one who brings Moab's pride low, which Balanced shows with the pronoun for God.

source.text: וּמִבְצַ֞ר מִשְׂגַּ֣ב חוֹמֹתֶ֗יךָ הֵשַׁ֥ח הִשְׁפִּ֛יל הִגִּ֥יעַ לָאָ֖רֶץ עַד־עָפָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the fortification of the refuge of your walls he will lay low, he will bring low, he will make touch to ground, to [the] dust.

en.L: And the fortress of the high refuge of your walls {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring down, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lay low, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make [it] touch the ground, to the dust.
en.B: Your high fortress with its towering walls {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will throw down; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will level it, bringing it to the ground, down into the dust.
en.R: Moab, your walls are high and strong, but God will tear them down. He will knock them flat on the ground, down into the dust.

decisions.choice: your walls: Moab addressed directly
decisions.reason: The verse turns to speak to Moab, whose high walls were its pride and its hope of safety.

decisions.choice: lay low, bring low, make touch the ground: the same verbs used of the lofty city in 26:5
decisions.reason: The three verbs return in 26:5 for the city on the heights. What God does to Moab's walls he does to every proud city.

decisions.choice: Moab; God
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed (Moab) and the one who acts (God), which the Hebrew leaves to the context.
